item.title: While Taliban leaders mark 5 years in power in Afghanistan, a UN official warns of a rights crisis
item.description:

Photo by Wakil Kohsar/AFP via Getty Images. Five years ago today, as the U.S. hurried to bring an end to its longest war and Afghanistan’s government collapsed, Taliban fighters swept into Kabul. item.description:

Photo by Zain Jaafar/AFP via Getty Images US Ambassador Mike Huckabee called settlers besieging a Palestinian American home in the occupied West Bank “ Israeli terrorists .” It’s a welcome, rare rebuke from a U.S. official, but what kind of weight does it really have when the same official has been a long-time supporter of Israeli settlements? item.title: The Orwellian Company Behind ICE’s New Electric Shock Gloves
item.description:
In 2022, Assistant Chief Adam Glueck, of the Cape Girardeau Police Department in southeastern Missouri, purchased electric shock gloves for his officers after learning about them at a trade show. And his employees, he said, couldn’t get enough of them. “If I try to take away the gloves from those officers at this point I think we may have a mutiny on our hands,” Glueck joked on a podcast interview a couple of years later. “They’ve grown really attached.”  The shock gloves, he went on to explain, allow their wearer to inflict pain without leaving the sort of marks that could look bad to witnesses or leave an officer vulnerable to lawsuits.  “In today’s society, you know, everybody’s filming everything, everybody has a cell phone,” Glueck said. item.title: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: One death every 30 minutes
item.description:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo spread to a sixth province as the overall death toll surpassed 2,100 and cases topped 4,500. Experts say the virus may have been transmitted undetected for months, while health workers have struggled to contain the outbreak with poor medical supplies and no approved vaccine for the new strain — though several are in the works. The head of the World Health Organization this week warned that the current outbreak threatens to be the biggest ever, with authorities playing catch-up to the disease after “ a big head start. ” During the previous deadliest outbreak, which killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016, authorities had recorded 755 cases at the same point . — Jeronimo Gonzalez

item.title: American missionary kidnapped in Niger freed after nine months
item.description:
An American missionary held in captivity in Niger for nine months will soon reunite with his family. Christian missionary pilot Kevin Rideout is free and safe with American officials after his kidnapping last year, his mission organization said Friday. It is not yet known how he escaped captivity or what group was holding him, but Islamist terror groups run rampant in Niger. Rideout, a father of four, was working with the Evangelical organization Serving in Mission (SIM) when he was kidnapped from Niamey, Niger, on October 21, 2025. “We are grateful to confirm that our good friend and brother in Christ, Kevin Rideout, has been released after over nine months in captivity,” the organization said in a statement. “Kevin is in good health in the care of US officials. item.title: Karoline Leavitt leaves behind a legacy of lies. What’s next for the Trump aide? | Arwa Mahdawi
item.description:
At the end of the month, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt will end a tenure that many consider to be one of the best in the 97-year history of the office. Importantly, she will leave something behind — a vital legacy of opening the briefing room to independent media. Leavitt handled her office with grace and dexterity, no mean feat for someone communicating for President Donald Trump , who talks more than a morning radio disc jockey. Somehow, she was never in front of his messaging, but also never far behind. As a queen of cool, Leavitt could not be flustered. She always had an air of confidence and, dare I say, levity. Even when her occasional jocular barbs were tossed at reporters, they rarely turned into acrimony. item.title: France’s top court rejects social media ban for under-15s
item.description:
France’s Constitutional Court has struck down a law that would have banned children under 15 from social media, ruling that it disproportionately infringed on freedom of expression and raised privacy concerns over age verification. The government plans to draft a revised bill, with Emmanuel Macron citing concerns over the impact of social media on children’s mental and physical health.

item.title: Zambia resumes vote count after pause over violence
